newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine court rejects MP's plea in rape case.
newsitem.headline: Philippine court rejects MP's plea in rape case.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court on Friday rejected the plea of a legislator accused of statutory rape of an 11-year-old girl to quash the charges against him and retract an order for his arrest.
The Supreme Court, saying it has no jurisdiction over the case, sent the petition of congressman Romeo Jalosjos to the Court of Appeals.

"There is no special and important reason for this court to take cognisance of this petition in the first instance," it said in answer to the legislator's plea to dismiss the two statutory rape charges and 12 counts of lasciviousness filed by government prosecutors 10 days ago.
Police said they were still unable to locate Jalosjos, a House of Representatives member from President Fidel Ramos's ruling coalition, who was ordered arrested on Thursday.

Judge Roberto Diokno of the Makati Regional Trial Court also recommended that bail not be given on the rape charges and stipulated that a bail of 40,000 pesos was set for each charge of committing acts of lasciviousness.
Justice Secretary Teofisto Guingona said the state would ask for the death penalty for Jalosjos.
Manila newspapers reported the case in August at a time of public uproar over crimes involving politicians and other prominent people thought to be beyond the reach of the law.

Prosecutors said in documents filed with the Makati Regional Trial court that the acts were committed in Jalosjos's Manila apartment. They said he paid the girl amounts ranging up to 10,000 pesos ($385) each time she visited him, and promised to make her a movie star.
The girl's father brought her to the politician in exchange for money, they said. The father faces a separate charge of child exploitation.
Jalosjos, in a petition filed in court by his lawyers last week, called the charges a "fairy tale" and accused prosecutors of bowing to media pressure "to satisfy one's appetite for blood."
